title: Drug Interaction Report – Patient A
content: Patient A is prescribed Warfarin (5 mg/day) and Aspirin (100 mg/day). Concomitant use significantly increases bleeding risk. The clinical team recommends monitoring INR weekly and adjusting the Warfarin dose accordingly.

title: Side Effects Summary – Metformin
content: Metformin is a first-line oral antidiabetic drug. Common side effects include gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, diarrhoea, and abdominal discomfort. Lactic acidosis is a rare but serious adverse effect. Vitamin B12 deficiency may develop with long-term use.

title: Clinical Trial Summary – NovaDrug X
content: Phase II trial of NovaDrug X enrolled 240 participants with Type 2 diabetes. The primary endpoint (HbA1c reduction at 24 weeks) was met by 68% of the treatment arm vs 22% placebo. Most common adverse event was headache (12%). No serious cardiac events recorded.

title: Contraindications – Warfarin
content: Warfarin is contraindicated in pregnancy, active bleeding disorders, haemorrhagic stroke within the past 3 months, and known hypersensitivity to coumarin derivatives. Caution required in elderly patients and those with renal or hepatic impairment.
